clue.text: Ruler here, pet target for bashing

indicators.note: something put up for bashing gets knocked about, so the letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone in charge picks out a favourite target to beat up.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'Ruler' from 'here', which belongs to the fodder; together 'here, pet target' supplies all thirteen letters of PETER THE GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter I was the tsar who modernised Russia, so he is a famous monarch and sovereign.

clue.text: Model runs into Fat Pang

indicators.note: one thing running into another ends up inside it

parts.note: Chris Patten, the last British governor of Hong Kong, was nicknamed Fat Pang there
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A model makes a dash towards a stout man called Pang.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat Pang looks like a made-up person, but it was the Cantonese nickname of Chris Patten, governor of Hong Kong until 1997. R goes into PATTEN to give PATTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or exemplar to be copied, which is one sense of a model.

clue.text: Play electronic dance music to entertain limitless Europeans

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other
without limits means the word loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: trance is a genre of electronic dance music
Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone puts on club music to keep some visitors from the continent amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like an instruction to put the music on, but it is the definition, in its mechanical sense of slack.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, play is the slack or allowed variation between parts, which is what a tolerance measures.

clue.text: Feature of much verse and church music, mostly used in religious studies

indicators.note: something used inside something else is placed within it

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hymn is a song sung in church

explanation.surface: A list of things found in poetry and in services, with a nod to how they turn up in RE lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: HYMN loses its last letter and HYM goes inside RE, the British school abbreviation for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching end sounds are a typical device of a great deal of poetry, hence a common characteristic of verse.

clue.text: Prominent feature film of the 90s: Basic Instinct?

parts.note: Hook is Spielberg's 1991 Peter Pan film
a nose for something is a natural, basic instinct for it

explanation.surface: A standout film of the nineties: was it Basic Instinct?
explanation.walkthrough: Basic Instinct really is a 90s film, which makes it look like the answer to 'film of the 90s'; the question mark flags that it is read as an ordinary phrase, a gut sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooked nose sticks out from the face, so it is a conspicuous facial characteristic, literally prominent.

clue.text: Rubberneckers gossip after popping by

indicators.note: after something is popped in, it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Nosy onlookers come to chat once someone has dropped by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popping by' reads as a casual visit, but 'popping' is the insertion and 'by' is the piece popped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gapers stare open-mouthed at an accident or spectacle, just as nosy rubberneckers crane to look.

clue.text: Elderly folk with urge to replace old kitchen gadgets

indicators.note: one word takes the place of another inside the phrase, swapping them over

parts.note: old-timers are elderly people
to egg on is to urge
taken as written: the word to be swapped out

explanation.surface: Pensioners are keen to throw out their worn-out kitchen equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: In OLD-TIMERS the word OLD is swapped for EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg timers are small sand-glasses or clocks used when boiling eggs, so they are kitchen devices.

clue.text: Names of parts of algebraic expressions from school days
Public service workers in harmony, though not technically

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the big British trade union for public sector staff
second meaning: together, everyone singing the same note

explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is the UK's largest union, for public service employees. Musically, unison means everyone on the same note, which strictly is not harmony; hence the setter's caveat.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use, acting in unison means in agreement, although in music it means singing one line rather than harmonising parts.

clue.text: Call for blood from unbelievable yahoo oddly

parts.note: a tall story is one hard to believe

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the odd positions of the word

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A shout for violence comes from some incredible lout.
explanation.walkthrough: A yahoo is a boor; here the word just supplies its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry on sighting the fox, a shout urging the pack on to the kill.

clue.text: Crude stuff produced by e.g. Berkshire press

parts.note: the Berkshire is a breed of pig
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Some unrefined material comes off a printing press in Berkshire, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire looks like the English county, but here it is a breed of pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is the impure metal straight from a blast furnace, before refining, so it is raw material.

clue.text: Headless porter? That's uncannily frightening

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ghostly porter without a head would be a spooky sight indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' looks like the start of the definition, but it supplies IE, the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling in a way that inspires a creeping fear of the supernatural.

clue.text: Being self-absorbed, Russians swimming will catch cold

indicators.note: what catches something holds it inside
swimming letters are moving about freely and so settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Swimmers from Russia, wrapped up in themselves, are bound to catch a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being self-absorbed' reads as a description of the Russians, but it is the definition: a being who is self-absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection, the archetype of vanity.

clue.text: Northern son seen recycling garbage

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade in a new form

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lad from the North of England is spotted sorting the rubbish for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbage' sits naturally with recycling, but it is the definition in its figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is used figuratively for rubbishy talk or ideas, which is just what nonsense is.

clue.text: Cryptic notices circulating round the northernmost part of Milton Keynes?

indicators.note: circulating round something means going all the way about it, enclosing it
cryptic writing is coded, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the anagram fodder
a round shape like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue the northernmost part of a word is its top, its first letter

parts.note: the top letter

explanation.surface: Mysterious signs are going round the north of the new town of Milton Keynes.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is a new town in England, but the clue splits it: Milton gives M, and Keynes is the definition, John Maynard Keynes.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the most influential British thinker on money and markets in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Stay on at sea

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: An order to keep sailing rather than come ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay on' looks like one phrase; 'on' belongs to the wordplay. 'At sea' gives MAIN, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to continue in the same place or state without leaving.

clue.text: Dance and sing about getting higher

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are shifted round into a different order

parts.note: taken as written for the fodder
taken as written for the fodder

explanation.surface: Performing a song-and-dance routine leaves you on a high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance and sing' look like instructions, but the two words are the fodder and 'about' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending means rising or climbing upward, going to a greater height.

clue.text: Follow Filipino around Norway

indicators.note: a word placed around another surrounds it

parts.note: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines, the basis of Filipino
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Instructions to shadow a man from the Philippines on a trip round Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: Filipino looks like a person, but it is the national language, which is standardised Tagalog.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to accompany someone, going behind them uninvited.

clue.text: Street wisdom about alcohol

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, read back to front

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Streetwise knowledge about booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcohol' suggests drink, but it is the chemical class: sterols such as cholesterol are alcohols.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterol is a steroid compound carrying a hydroxyl group, which makes it a member of the chemical alcohols.

clue.text: Lord Coe impressed by Portuguese saint in Japanese port

indicators.note: something impressed by another is pressed into it, ending up inside

parts.note: São is Portuguese for saint, as in São Paulo
Sebastian Coe, the Olympic runner, is known as Seb

explanation.surface: An athletics peer is wowed by a Portuguese holy man at a harbour in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Coe is Sebastian Coe, double Olympic 1500m champion and later head of the London 2012 Games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasebo is a city and naval harbour in Nagasaki prefecture, on the island of Kyushu.

clue.text: Bears with footwear and cushions

parts.note: to bear something is to have it
socks are worn on the feet; with joins them on

explanation.surface: Bears in socks with pillows sounds like a scene from a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, but it is the verb, as in bears a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassocks are thick padded kneeling cushions found in churches.

clue.text: Small dog's arrogant style of perambulation

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a dog is jokingly a wagger, as it wags its tail

explanation.surface: A little dog struts along self-importantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'dog's' is just the link 'is'; the dog is pictured as a wagger, one that wags its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to walk with a bold, conceited strut, so a swagger is a cocky way of walking.

clue.text: Old family bones brought to Italy

parts.note: Bones is slang for a doctor, from Star Trek's Dr McCoy
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Ancestral remains are carried back to the family's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' suggests skeletons, but it is slang for a doctor, as with 'Bones' McCoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the banking dynasty who ruled Florence for centuries, a famous historic family.

clue.text: Very long time needed to catch each TV series

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
an era is a long period
a pop means each, as in a pound a pop

explanation.surface: Getting through every episode of a show takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very long time' looks like one phrase; it splits into 'Very' and 'long time', which together go around 'each'. 'A pop' is British slang for each, apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television, so it is a kind of programme run.

clue.text: Tart wears a new garment that only covers the front of body

definitions.text: garment that only covers the front of body

indicators.note: what one wears is put around one, so the outer piece goes around the first

parts.note: a taken as written, plus N for new
tart and pro are both slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A streetwalker puts on a new outfit that is skimpy behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' could be a pastry, which fits a kitchen garment, but here it is slang for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is tied on to protect clothes, hanging down in front with the back left open.

clue.text: Some hitman in Japan?

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A question about one particular contract killer in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a ninja was a covert Japanese assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were feudal Japanese agents trained in espionage and assassination, effectively killers for hire.

clue.text: Ex-PM picked up female on the game

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
RU is rugby union, often called the game

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was caught with a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute; here 'on' just places one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, from independence until 1964.

clue.text: Baroque sculptor from Swiss city, fashionable one

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
in means trendy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trendy artist from Switzerland is said to be a great Baroque master.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the leading Italian sculptor and architect of seventeenth-century Rome.

clue.text: Old church bell needs colouring brownish-yellow

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
CH is the abbreviation for church
a bell is a phone call, as in give me a bell, so a ring

explanation.surface: An ancient church bell needs repainting a mustard shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like the church fitting, but here it is British slang for a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a brownish-yellow earth pigment, so ochring means tinting something that colour.

clue.text: Duck at McDonald's? It's overhyped in America

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero
what you get at McDonald's

explanation.surface: Is a duck dish at a fast-food chain all hype?
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batter's score of nothing. The definition is the whole last phrase: an American term for something hyped but trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothingburger is US slang for an issue or event that gets lots of attention but turns out insignificant.
